back: A data structure holding a fixed number of items of the same type under one identifier, reached by an index.
An element is one item in an array; its index is the number giving its position.
The smallest and largest valid index. An index outside them is an error.
ARRAY[1:n] OF type for 1D; ARRAY[1:r, 1:c] OF type for 2D (r rows, c columns).
A loop with the loop variable as the index: total, maximum, count or search.
Nested loops: the outer for the rows and the inner for the columns; the element is Array[Row, Col].
Counting starts at 0, so pseudocode Marks[4] is marks[3]; a 2D array is a list of lists, scores[row][col].
Static (array): fixed size, elements stored together, quick access. Dynamic (linked list, tree): size changes as the program runs.
A list of one kind of value: 1D. A table where each value needs two characteristics: 2D.
